critical_issues: CRITICAL (OQ1 — analysis UNSOUND as specified, blocks coding): The decidable missing-barrier HARD ERROR (A.4.1, HirError::SharedMissingBarrierBeforeCrossInvocationRead) keys ONLY on shared-id X — 'a SharedWrite of shared-id X followed by a SharedRead of the SAME id X in the same block with no intervening barrier'. It does NOT distinguish the read INDEX from the write INDEX, and therefore does NOT distinguish a CROSS-invocation read (the real NVIDIA-passes/AMD-races trap, which reads a DIFFERENT cell than written: `tile[lid]=v; barrier; ...=tile[other]`) from a SAME-invocation SELF-read of the invocation's OWN cell (`tile[lid]=v; let w=tile[lid]+1.0;` — needs NO barrier; program-order visibility within one invocation is guaranteed). As written, the hard error FALSE-POSITIVES the same-index self-read, which is a CORRECT kernel. The architect's explicit 'zero false positives' justification for choosing HARD ERROR over advisory warning is therefore NOT met. FIX (must be specified before coding): the hard error may fire ONLY when the read index is NOT provably equal to the write index (e.g. syntactically distinct index expressions, or any index the analysis cannot prove identical); when the read index is provably the same SSA value/expression as the most-recent write index, it is a safe same-invocation self-read and must be EXCLUDED (no error, no warning). Conservatively: if index-equality is undecidable, DEMOTE to the advisory warning rather than hard-error, to preserve the zero-false-positive guarantee that justifies the hard error. Update A.4.1 + the typecheck.rs change item + AT to encode the (id X, index-disequality) key and add a positive test that `tile[i]=v; let w=tile[i];` (same index, same block, no barrier) does NOT hard-error.
warnings: WARNING (OQ2 — mechanism under-specified for while-loops; shipped kernels SAFE): divergent_context_depth (typecheck.rs:545) is a SINGLE counter incremented by if-then (956), if-else (965), AND while (1174) — but NOT by for-range (per the line-543/544 doc-comment; check_for_stmt at 998 pushes only loop_stack, no depth increment). The architect's A.4.2 rule requires distinguishing 'enclosing divergent frame is an if/else body (ERROR)' from 'loop-introduced depth (OK)'. A bare `divergent_context_depth > 0` check CANNOT make that distinction: it would correctly reject if/else-nested barriers and correctly accept for-range-nested barriers (depth 0 — the SHIPPED matmul/attention K-loops use `for ... in range(...)`, VERIFIED in existing examples/matmul_tile.axc + q4km_dequant_matmul.axc, so they are depth 0 and NEVER flagged — the no-false-positive-on-legitimate-kernels requirement IS met), BUT it would also reject a barrier inside a `while`-loop body (depth>0), which A.4.2 itself says should be PERMITTED ('for/while-body where the loop trip count is workgroup-uniform = OK'). No shipped kernel uses `while`, so this is a bounded, safe-by-default over-rejection — NOT a correctness hole and NOT a blocker. But the architect must either (a) add one sentence telling the Coder the concrete discriminator (e.g. a separate `if_else_depth` counter incremented ONLY at if/then/else, flag the barrier iff if_else_depth>0; loop_stack already tracks loop frames separately), so AT-1635's 'uniform-loop-barrier accepted' half also holds for while-loops, OR (b) explicitly document that M3.2 conservatively rejects ALL barriers at divergent_context_depth>0 including while-bodies (a known, documented over-rejection). As written, the changelog ('flag while divergent_context_depth > 0 in an if/else body') names infra that cannot detect 'in an if/else body' specifically — clarify the mechanism.
